system: You are an expert reviewer of machine-learning research ideas.
user:
Compare two research ideas for the SAME research problem and pick the stronger one.

Research problem: In MVFA's few-shot inference, the released code min-max normalises the zero-shot (text) branch and the few-shot (memory-bank) branch with the minimum and maximum over the entire test set and adds them with a fixed weight of 0.5, so the score of one image depends on the rest of the test set and a single incoming image cannot be scored. Can this transductive normalisation be replaced by an inductive one computed only from the K normal support images, at a small cost in AUROC? The inductive normaliser maps each branch's patch scores through the 1st and 99th percentiles of the leave-one-out patch scores of the supports (every patch of support i scored against the memory bank of the other K-1 supports and against the text anchors), which gives thousands of reference values even at K = 2; the fusion weight and the max pooling of the image score are kept fixed. Primary outcome: image-level and pixel-level AUROC of inductive versus transductive normalisation on each held-out BMAD dataset for K in {2, 4, 8, 16}. Motivating measurement: the spread of the original method's AUROC across random half-size test subsets and at shifted prevalence (10% and 50% abnormal). Secondary outcome: sensitivity at 95% specificity with a threshold fixed from the support scores alone.

A stronger idea is one whose proposed change acts on the SPECIFIC mechanism of the target method that causes the problem (here: the released MVFA code and its verified behaviour), rather than a generic improvement that would apply to any anomaly detector.

Judge on:
1. Specificity. Would this idea plausibly solve THIS problem in THIS method better than a generic alternative? A mechanism that applies equally to any model and any problem is WEAKER, not stronger, because it does not explain why it fixes this problem.
2. Evidence. Is the proposed mechanism supported by the cited literature or by verified properties of the code and the benchmark?
3. Testability. Does the idea make a concrete, falsifiable prediction that can be checked on BMAD with one Colab GPU?

Explicitly DO NOT reward: length or polish of the write-up, stacking many modules, vague "add an attention/adapter module" proposals, or ideas that need data, labels or compute that are not available.

Idea A:
TITLE: Extreme-value tail extension of the support CDF
SUMMARY: Model the upper tail of each branch's leave-one-out support scores with a generalised Pareto distribution, so scores beyond the largest support value are still ordered instead of all mapping to 1, which matters because the image score is the maximum of the fused map.
HYPOTHESIS: Replacing the saturated top of the empirical CDF with a generalised-Pareto tail fitted above the 90th support percentile increases image AUROC by at least 1 point over the plain empirical CDF at K <= 4, where the fraction of test images whose max fused score is tied at the ceiling exceeds 20%.
RATIONALE: An empirical CDF is flat at 1 above the largest reference value. With few supports, many test patches — in normal and abnormal images alike — exceed every support score, so after max pooling a large share of test images obtain the same ceiling score and AUROC loses resolution exactly where it matters. Extreme value theory gives a principled extrapolation: exceedances over a high threshold follow a generalised Pareto distribution, whose parameters can be fitted from the support scores above their 90th percentile (thousands of patches even at K = 2). The resulting CDF is strictly increasing in the tail and remains test-set invariant.
METHOD: 1) utils.py: fit_gpd(R, q=0.9) by maximum likelihood (scipy.stats.genpareto) per branch and level. 2) F(s) = ECDF(s) for s <= u; F(s) = 0.9 + 0.1 x GPD_cdf(s - u) above the threshold u. 3) test_few.py: apply per branch and level; 0.5 fusion and max pooling unchanged; test-set min-max removed. 4) Report the fraction of tied image scores. No training.
EXPERIMENT: Leave-one-modality-out on BMAD (RESC and OCT17 held out together), MVFA retrained with source-validation selection; K in {2, 4, 8, 16}; 3 seeds x 3 support draws; 0.5 fusion and max pooling unchanged. Baselines: transductive MVFA pipeline, support percentiles (problem statement). Additional baseline: plain LOO empirical CDF. Metrics: AUROC, fraction of tied image scores. Falsified if no AUROC gain at K <= 4 where ties exceed 20%.

Idea B:
TITLE: Alignment-adaptive residual CDF: weighting the positional correction by measured anatomy alignment
SUMMARY: Use the residual empirical CDF (positional median subtracted, global CDF of residuals) but weight the positional correction by how much the supports' normal scores actually vary with position, so unaligned modalities fall back to the plain global CDF automatically.
HYPOTHESIS: The alignment-adaptive residual CDF is never worse than the global empirical CDF by more than 0.3 pixel-AUROC points on any held-out dataset, and on spatially aligned datasets it keeps at least 80% of the full residual-CDF gain, at all K.
RATIONALE: The global-CDF parent is safe but ignores anatomy; the residual-CDF parent removes anatomy offsets but assumes alignment. Their combination measures alignment from the supports themselves: the share of variance of leave-one-out support scores explained by grid position (an intraclass correlation, rho). The positional correction is applied with weight rho, so a modality whose normal score level does not depend on position (ChestXray crops, histopathology tiles) receives the plain global CDF and a well-aligned one receives the residual CDF.
METHOD: 1) utils.py: rho = var_between_positions / (var_between + var_within) of LOO support scores per branch and level (positions pooled in 3x3 neighbourhoods). 2) Residual r = s_j - rho x med_j (med_j shrunk positional median); reference set built from support LOO residuals computed the same way. 3) test_few.py: F(r) via searchsorted; 0.5 fusion and max pooling unchanged; test-set min-max removed. No training.
EXPERIMENT: Leave-one-modality-out on BMAD (RESC and OCT17 held out together), MVFA retrained with source-validation selection; K in {2, 4, 8, 16}; 3 seeds x 3 support draws; 0.5 fusion and max pooling unchanged. Baselines: transductive MVFA pipeline, support percentiles (problem statement). Additional baselines: global empirical CDF; residual CDF with rho = 1. Report rho per dataset. Falsified if the adaptive variant is worse than the global CDF by more than 0.3 points on any dataset.

Respond in exactly this format:
REASONING: <one to three sentences explaining your choice>
CONFIDENCE: <HIGH | MEDIUM | LOW>
WINNER=<A | B | TIE>
response:
REASONING: Idea A directly diagnoses and fixes the exact failure mode that arises when moving from whole-test-set min-max normalization to support-only normalization combined with image-level max pooling: saturation at the upper bound causing tied image anomaly scores. In contrast, Idea B introduces a generic spatial-alignment heuristic borrowed from general visual anomaly detection without directly resolving the specific support-normalization-to-max-pooling issue of MVFA.
CONFIDENCE: HIGH
WINNER=A
